newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila firms seen buying more corn/wheat next week.
newsitem.headline: Manila firms seen buying more corn/wheat next week.

text.p: Philippine firms are expected to shop for more corn and wheat in the coming week to meet their short-term requirements, traders said on Friday.
The state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) announced it would tender for 150,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn no 2 or its equivalent on October 29.
The NFA plans to sell the imported corn to local feed millers and poultry and hog farmers.
"We have advised traders that we are looking for U.S. yellow corn number 2, with shipments originating either from the U.S. Pacific Northwest, Gulf or Argentina," an NFA official told Reuters.
Philippine traders said they have been informed that the NFA wants the shipment to arrive in December.
Livestock farmers said 150,000 tonnes is not enough to meet their requirements up to the first quarter of 1997.

Philippine Association of Hog Raisers Inc president Soledad Agbayani told reporters feed millers, hog and poultry raisers have asked the Department of Agriculture to import another 250,000 tonnes of corn on top of the 150,000 tonnes.
This will help make up for shortfalls in local supply between the last quarter of this year up to March 1997.
Since the start of the year, Philippines has imported 250,000 tonnes of corn for animal feed, all of it from the United States and Argentina.

Traders said the prevailing price of yellow whole grain corn for feeds dropped to 7.0 pesos (26.71 cents) from 7.20 (27.48 cents) per kg while the prevailing retail price of white whole grain corn used in making starch edged up to 7.30 pesos (27.9) from 7.20 pesos (27.48 cents) per kg.
Philippine firms are also expected to come back for more wheat if prices soften further, traders said.
On Friday, two firms told commodity houses that they were in the market for a total of 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

A day before that, a Philippine food manufacturer and flour miller bought 11,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with a 13.5 percent protein content at $4.10 per bushel FOB, and another 6,000 tonnes of western white wheat at $4.0 per bushel FOB, traders said.
The firm also bought 6,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean at over $200 per tonne FOB for mid-November shipment.

Another Philippine miller also clinched a deal for 8,500 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with a 14 percent protein content at $4.10 per bushel, and another 8,500 tonnes of western white wheat at $4.00 per bushel.
The price did not include freight, traders said.

Traders said prevailing retail price of a 25 kg bag of hard wheat flour in Metro Manila dropped to 290 pesos ($11.06) from last week's 300 pesos ($11.45) while the prevailing retail price of soft wheat flour remained unchanged at 260 pesos ($9.92).
